text:
max: CI alert — onboarding-tests failing across the matrix. Vitest passes locally but jest in CI errors out with 'Cannot use import statement outside a module'.
build-bot: nightly-onboarding  build/onboarding #1203 failed
```
Error: Cannot use import statement outside a module
    at Object.compileFunction (node:vm:360:18)
    at Module._compile (internal/modules/cjs/loader:1092:27)
```

leah: root cause looks like conditional exports in @redwood/sdk: import -> dist/runtime.mjs, require -> dist/runtime.cjs. Test runners resolve different export targets so our fetch/kv mocks attach to different module identities.
eo: repro locally: `pnpm -w test --filter=@redwood/sdk -- run unit`. Vitest (vite resolver) picks the import entry; jest + transformIgnorePatterns ends up loading the cjs. Result: mocks patch one module object and the other runner doesn't see them.

max: minimal fixes that worked for CI in infra:
1) Add a tiny CJS test shim `tests/shim/runtime.cjs` that uses createRequire to load the CJS runtime, e.g.:
```js
// tests/shim/runtime.cjs
const { createRequire } = require('module');
const req = createRequire(import.meta.url || __filename);
module.exports = req('../../dist/runtime.cjs');
```
2) vitest.config.ts: inline the package so Vite doesn't fold to import entry:
```ts
export default defineConfig({ test: { deps: { inline: ['@redwood/sdk'] } } })
```
3) jest.config.js: map the package to the shim and allow transform:
```js
module.exports = {
  transformIgnorePatterns: ['node_modules/(?!@redwood/sdk)'],
  moduleNameMapper: { '^@redwood/sdk$': '<rootDir>/tests/shim/runtime.cjs' }
}
```

leah: also added `types` root + `exports.types` so TypeScript and ts-jest pick up runtime typings regardless of which export path the resolver chooses. That removed a bunch of noisy `any` issues in onboarding sample apps.
eo: alternate longer-term options discussed: publish a small dev-only `@redwood/runtime-testing` package that's CJS-only and re-exports the mock hooks. Consumers/dev-deps can import that in tests so both runners get the same module identity. Cleaner than shimming package exports in each repo.

max: opened PR https://git.internal/redwood/sdk/pull/990 with the shim + vitest inline change + a short DEVEX doc. CI green on linux/mac; Windows still shows a path-length flake but much reduced failure rate.

rafael: one more gotcha: monorepo hoisting + re-exports can create duplicate copies of the runtime if consumers import via different paths (e.g., `@redwood/sdk` vs `@redwood/sdk/runtime`). Recommend normalizing imports to `@redwood/sdk/runtime` in sample apps and tests.

max: I'll add a short wiki page "Testing ESM packages with Vitest & Jest" with recipes: shim pattern, vitest deps.inline, jest moduleNameMapper + transformIgnorePatterns, and types/exports tips. Linking PR in the doc. Closing unless new stack traces appear. :white_check_mark:
